items.summary: Playing in his first game since Week 11 of last season, Penix started off sluggishly Thursday before finding a rhythm and putting together a near-flawless performance. Penix threw his one interception four plays into the night on a pass intended for Jahan Dotson, but he went on to record only five more incompletions the rest of the way while connecting with Austin Hooper for a five-yard touchdown pass just before halftime. Penix's chemistry with Drake London also was in fine form over the last three quarters, and he hit his No. 1 target for gains of 68 and 40 yards in the fourth quarter to help close out the upset victory. Penix should only get more comfortable the further removed he is from the third ACL surgery of his playing career, and he'll look to carry over the considerable momentum from his season debut into a Week 4 road divisional showdown against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

items.summary: Keenum's final numbers underscore how effective he was running Ben Johnson's aggressive offense against a quality defense. The 38-year-old signal-caller, who got the starting nod over Tyson Bagent in Caleb Williams' (hamstring) stead, connected with seven different targets overall, facilitating multi-reception tallies for four of his pass catchers. Goff has tossed multiple touchdowns in three straight games to begin the year, completing 70.6 percent of his passes (77-for-109) for 802 yards and a stellar 8:0 TD:INT. He'll look to keep rolling in a Week 4 road clash against the Panthers.

items.headline: Lawrence completed 19 of 29 passes for 182 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 25 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.summary: Lawrence's passing yardage continued its downward trend for the second straight game, but the 2021 first overall pick threw multiple touchdown passes for the second time to open the season. He connected with Josh Cameron (12 yards), Jakobi Meyers (10 yards) and Parker Washington (17 yards) for his trio of scoring tosses, and he offered solid supplemental fantasy production with his legs. Lawrence will take 616 passing yards and a 7:2 TD:INT into a Week 4 road showdown against Joe Burrow and the Bengals next Sunday.

items.summary: Kolar remains unlikely to play Sunday against the Seahawks, as he continues his recovery from a broken forearm, which he suffered in Week 2. Oronde Gadsden, Hayden Rucci and Patrick Herbert handled tight-end duties against the Bills last Sunday.

items.summary: Justin Herbert's top target turned in a solid stat line in the Chargers' third straight loss to open the season, yet it still wasn't enough to net Los Angeles its first win. McConkey finished second in receptions and receiving yards while slotting in third in targets on the afternoon for the Bolts, but through three contests, he sports a modest 12-183-1 line on 15 targets. It doesn't get any easier for the Chargers in Week 4, as they pay a visit to the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday afternoon.

items.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said that Douglas (ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Travis Wingfield of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hafley labeled Douglas as day-to-day when he spoke to the media Monday, but the rookie wideout apparently hasn't made enough progress in his recovery from the ankle injury two days later to practice in any fashion. Considering he missed the Dolphins' Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, Douglas will probably need to put in a full practice by Friday in order to approach Sunday's game in Minnesota without a designation.

items.summary: Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas will miss Sunday's game against the Chiefs, coach Jeff Hafley said Friday, leaving Miami without its leading receiver for at least this week.

items.headline: Gordon rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all three of his targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 24-10 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Gordon capitalized on his added opportunities after De'Von Achane (knee) exited the game in the first quarter. The 2025 sixth-round pick capped Miami's 17-play, 91-yard opening drive with a three-yard touchdown run, one play after Gordon converted a third-and-9 with an 11-yard run. Miami's offense produced just three points the rest of the way and Gordon exited briefly due to cramps but returned. Achane is feared to have a major injury, and if Jaylen Wright (foot) is also unable to play against the Vikings in Week 3, Gordon would be in line to handle a substantial workload again in the Dolphins' struggling offense.

items.headline: Wentz will serve as the Vikings' backup quarterback Sunday against the Buccaneers after head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Monday that Kyler Murray has cleared concussion protocol and will start Week 3.
items.summary: Wentz performed admirably across nearly two full games in relief of Murray, who sustained the concussion midway through the first quarter of the season opener against the Packers. After completing 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns in the Vikings' come-from-behind 39-22 win over Green Bay, Wentz started Week 2 against the Bears and played turnover-free football in rainy and windy conditions en route to leading Minnesota to a 9-3 win. While Murray will reclaim the starting job now that he's out of the protocol, Wentz's performance over the past two weeks firmly solidifies him ahead of 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy on the depth chart.

items.headline: Vikings to start QB Wentz vs. Bears with Murray still on the mend
items.summary: Carson Wentz will be the Vikings' starting quarterback Sunday against the Bears while Kyler Murray continues to work his way back after suffering a concussion in the season opener.

items.headline: Kamara carried the ball nine times for 36 yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders.
items.summary: The veteran RB once again took a back seat to Travis Etienne to begin the game, but that changed after the former Jaguar aggravated a hamstring strain and left the game in the third quarter. Over the Saints' last five possessions, Kamara split the workload in the backfield with Kendre Miller, getting six touches to Miller's five. The severity of Etienne's injury isn't yet clear, but if he misses significant time, Kamara and Miller would likely continue working in tandem, with rookie CJ Donaldson also potentially mixing in as a short-yardage option.

items.headline: Saints' Alvin Kamara practices, 'moving well' after MCL sprain
items.summary: Saints running back Alvin Kamara has "no limitations," was a full participant in practice and says his knee feels good only one month after spraining his MCL in practice.

items.headline: Saints' Alvin Kamara practices in full, 'in a great place'
items.summary: Saints coach Kellen Moore said he "feels good" about Alvin Kamara's chance of playing Sunday. The veteran RB was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.

items.headline: Shough completed 29 of 42 passes for 255 yards and four touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders. He added 36 rushing yards on his lone carry but also lost two fumbles.
items.summary: The second-year QB was dynamic once again, tossing two TDs each to tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, but protection issues in the absence of left tackle Kelvin Banks (ankle) ending up proving costly as all four of the Saints' fourth-quarter possessions ended in turnovers, causing them to squander a 27-22 lead. Shough has thrown eight touchdowns through three games but has also given the ball away six times (three INTs and three lost fumbles), and he'll try to clean up those issues in Week 4 at home against the Falcons.

items.headline: Tyler Shough, dubbed 'poor man' by Saints, leads win vs. Ravens
items.summary: After Ravens DC Anthony Weaver attempted to pay Saints QB Tyler Shough a compliment by referring to him as a "poor man's Josh Allen," the New Orleans coaches turned it into a joke, dubbing Shough "poor man" for the rest of the week.

items.headline: Saints QB Tyler Shough expects less jitters vs. Ravens

items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (thigh) won't practice Wednesday and confirmed the running back is being viewed as week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Though Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday that an MRI on the quad injury Hall sustained in Sunday's loss to the Lions wasn't as significant as the Jets had feared, the running back appears likely to miss at least one game. Unless Hall is able to fit in some practice activity Thursday or Friday, the Jets will likely officially rule him out ahead of Sunday's contest in Chicago. Hall's expected absence would clear the way for Braelon Allen to serve as the Jets' lead option on the ground, while Isaiah Davis would likely be in store for added work in a change-of-pace role.

items.headline: Sources: Jets RB Breece Hall week-to-week with quad injury
items.summary: Jets running back Breece Hall, who suffered a quad injury in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions, is considered week-to-week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

items.headline: RB Breece Hall suffers thigh injury as Jets lose late again
items.summary: Jets running back Breece Hall suffered an injury to his right thigh late in Sunday's loss to the Lions.

items.headline: Ertz reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Ertz brought in one of two targets for nine yards during Monday's 27-7 loss at Chicago. It was a mostly uneventful reunion with his old team, but given that he was just signed a week ago, it's relatively impressive he led Philadelphia's tight ends in targets. With Dallas Goedert (knee) lacking a clear return date and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers (hamstring) still on IR, Ertz has a good chance of being added to the gameday roster again for a Week 4 matchup versus the Rams.

items.headline: Eagles reuniting with Zach Ertz as Dallas Goedert has MCL sprain
items.summary: The Eagles are signing tight end Zach Ertz to their practice squad after the injury to starter Dallas Goedert and other injuries at the position.

items.headline: Smith secured six of eight targets for 65 yards in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
items.summary: Smith led the Eagles across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets on a night when Jalen Hurts passed for just 153 yards. All three of the speedy wideout's totals also qualified as his second highest of the first three games of the season. Smith appears to be adjusting well to new coordinator Sean Mannion's offense despite the Eagles' collective performance on that side of the ball leaving plenty to be desired, and he'll take a robust 19-235-1 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 home showdown against the Rams on Sunday.

items.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith is headed into another stratosphere
items.summary: The Eagles' go-to guy in key moments has always seen himself as WR1 -- now everyone else is just catching up.

items.headline: Week 2 winners and losers: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, CeeDee Lamb shine; Bijan Robinson struggles
items.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and CeeDee Lamb came up big in Week 2, while Bijan Robinson and Justin Jefferson had very quiet days.

items.headline: Pittman caught two passes on five targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.summary: Pittman was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a foot injury. Despite the low offensive output, he played 45 of 62 offensive snaps (72.3 percent), which was second-most among Steelers wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (56). Pittman also was tied for the second-most targets, though six Pittsburgh pass catchers were targeted at least four times by Aaron Rodgers. Pittman has a 5-74-0 receiving line (eight targets) across two regular-season contests heading into Thursday's game against the Browns, whose secondary could be without starters Grant Delpit (shoulder) and Tyson Campbell (knee).

items.headline: Steelers rule out WR Pittman Jr. vs. Patriots with foot injury
items.summary: The Steelers will be without another starter for their Week 2 game against the Patriots after downgrading wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. to out with a foot injury.

items.headline: Joey Porter Jr. out again for Steelers; WR Pittman questionable
items.summary: The Steelers will be without top cornerback Joey Porter Jr. again amid their contentious contract negotiation. Wide receiver Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and offensive tackle Troy Fautanu (ankle) are questionable to play.

items.headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (ribs) won't practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
items.summary: Evans was laboring after taking a big hit from Cardinals safety Budda Baker in the second quarter of this past Sunday's win against Arizona, eventually being ruled out due to a rib injury. Afterward, Evans was diagnosed with a strained rib, but Shanahan also relayed to Vic Tafur of The Athletic on Wednesday that the wide receiver "may" practice later this week. Logging some on-field work Thursday and/or Friday seemingly will give Evans a chance to play Week 4 against the Broncos, but his upcoming availability remains up in the air.

items.headline: Evans, Williams, Greenlaw don't have long-term injuries, 49ers say
items.summary: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that injuries sustained by Mike Evans, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw on Sunday aren't considered long-term issues.

items.headline: Lock will return to a backup role for Sunday's game at Washington after coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Sam Darnold (glute) is "going to play," John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
items.summary: After Darnold suffered a right glute injury on Seattle's first possession of the season Week 1 against the Patriots, Lock directed the offense for the next seven-plus quarters, leading the team to two victories while completing 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and rushing twice for 13 yards. With Darnold back in action this weekend, though, Lock's time as the starter is over for now.

items.headline: Lock, Smith-Njigba have Seahawks 2-0 with Darnold ahead of schedule
items.summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold could return to practice this week and did not rule out the possibility of him playing next Sunday. In the meantime, backup Drew Lock has Seattle 2-0, with plenty of help from receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

items.headline: Drew Lock: Taking care of football key in Seahawks start
items.summary: As Drew Lock steps into a starting role for the Seattle Seahawks, the veteran quarterback knows he doesn't have to force the issue while he fills in for the injured Sam Darnold.

items.headline: Seahawks' Mike Macdonald says team still believes in RB Jadarian Price
items.summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said the team has not lost faith in starting running back Jadarian Price after the rookie first-round pick lost a fumble for the second week in a row Sunday.

items.headline: Price carried the ball five times for 15 yards and caught one of three targets for seven yards in Sunday's 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
items.summary: The Seahawks' running game continues to struggle, and Price's inability to make a consistent impact is causing him to lose touches. After seeing double-digit carries in each of his first two NFL games, the rookie's six touches trailed both Emanuel Wilson (nine carries) and George Holani (three totes and five catches). The chest injury Price suffered in Week 2 may have played a role in that distribution, but he hadn't topped 60 scrimmage yards or found the end zone in either of the first two weeks. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting closer to his 2026 debut, time may be running out for Price to establish himself in the lead role before the backfield gets even more crowded. He'll try to get going in a Week 4 home tilt against the Chargers.

items.headline: Seahawks encouraged by Jadarian Price leading RB room
items.summary: Seattle's running back committee has no touchdowns through two weeks, but there's another opportunity this week at Commanders.

items.headline: McLaurin caught six of nine targets for 77 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seahawks.
items.summary: After two frustrating games to begin the season that saw multiple near misses in the end zone, McLaurin finally broke out with Marcus Mariota under center instead of Jayden Daniels (elbow), hauling in a 30-yard strike in the third quarter of Sunday's upset. McLaurin led the Commanders in catches, targets and receiving yards in the win, and he'll take a 10-141-1 line on 22 targets into a Week 4 home tilt against the Colts.

items.summary: The veteran traveled with the team to London but still has some hurdles to clear before he returns to the field. Okonkwo has been sidelined with a hamstring injury since the season opener. It's worth noting that Wednesday's practice was a walkthrough, so this report was only an estimation. Thursday's session will shed more light on Okonkwo's status heading into the Week 4 matchup against the Colts. Fellow tight end Ben Sinnott was also estimated as limited due to a rib injury.

items.headline: Commanders rule RG Cosmi, TE Okonkwo, LB Luvu out Sunday
items.summary: Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) won't play Sunday vs. the Seahawks.

items.headline: Cardinals rookie Jeremiyah Love earns bigger role in offense
items.summary: The running back out of Notre Dame rushed 21 times for 90 yards and caught five passes, including a TD.

items.headline: Love rushed 21 times for 90 yards and brought in all five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Sunday may have marked the official crowning of Love as the Cardinals' unquestioned lead back, as he took 19 more carries than veteran backup Tyler Allgeier. All of Love's rush attempts, rushing yardage, receptions, receiving yardage and targets were new career-high figures for the rookie first-round pick, who also recorded his first receiving touchdown on a one-yard grab early in the fourth quarter. His draft pedigree and talent always made an ascension to the No. 1 role a matter of when and not if, and it will be interesting to see how the Notre Dame product fares in what could be a favorable Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

items.headline: Pitts secured one of two targets for five yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: Pitts' slow start persisted Thursday despite Michael Penix making his season debut and taking the reins of the offense from the ineffective duo of Cooper Rush and Jack Strand. Pitts has managed just two receptions for 20 yards on six targets through three games, but given how sharp Penix looked right out of the gate Thursday, the duo is bound to start clicking in coming games as they've done previously.

items.headline: Bateman caught two of three targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.summary: Bateman finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Zay Flowers, who compiled 84 receiving yards in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Bateman stepped up with seven catches for 88 yards and a touchdown while Flowers was sidelined in Week 2, but Flowers is the clear No. 1 option in Baltimore's wide receiver room, as Bateman was held without a catch when Flowers was active for the season opener. Up next for Bateman and the Ravens will be a Week 4 home game against the Titans.

items.headline: Kincaid secured two of three targets for 38 yards and lost a fumble in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
items.summary: Kincaid finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the afternoon for the Bills and tied for the same slotting in targets, but the tight end's downturn in production compared to the first two weeks stood out. He had opened the season with a combined 12-125-1 line on 14 targets, but the Chargers appeared to key on slowing him down Sunday and also forced the ball from him at the end of a 24-yard catch late in the third quarter for Kincaid's first lost fumble since his 2023 rookie campaign. Despite the relatively quiet performance, Kincaid should remain a key figure in the air attack during a Week 4 home matchup against the Patriots next Sunday.

items.headline: The Panthers listed Coker as a non-participant on Wednesday's practice estimate, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Carolina held a walk-through session for its first Week 4 practice, and though Coker was in attendance for the workout, he looked to be rehabbing off to the side, per Joe Person of The Athletic. Coker had previously appeared on injury reports in Weeks 2 and 3 due to an ankle injury, but he's now tending to a minor quad strain, which knocked him out of this past Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns. Per Alex Zietlow of The Charlotte Observer, head coach Dave Canales said he's viewing Coker as day-to-day, so the wideout should have a decent chance at suiting up this Sunday versus the Lions so long as he can practice in some capacity Thursday and/or Friday.

items.headline: Panthers scratch LB Devin Lloyd; WRs Coker, Legette questionable
items.summary: The Panthers will be without starting linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf) against the Browns, while wide receivers Jalen Coker (ankle) and Xavier Legette (knee) have been listed as questionable.

items.headline: Legette (knee) did not practice Wednesday, Alex Zietlow of The Charlotte Observer reports.
items.summary: Coach Dave Canales labeled Legette as week-to-week headed into Sunday night's game against the Lions. With Jalen Coker (quad) also dinged up, the Panthers could again be looking at giving Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie considerable playing time alongside Tetairoa McMillan in Detroit. Legette has a 2-64-0 receiving line on six targets across two games this season.

items.headline: Panthers scratch LB Devin Lloyd; WRs Coker, Legette questionable
items.summary: The Panthers will be without starting linebacker Devin Lloyd (calf) against the Browns, while wide receivers Jalen Coker (ankle) and Xavier Legette (knee) have been listed as questionable.

items.headline: Young (knee) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
items.summary: Young played every snap in this past Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Browns, but he made a visit to the blue medical tent on the Carolina sideline at one point during the contest to get his knee checked out. The knee issue evidently isn't a concern heading into Week 4, when Young and the Panthers will be preparing to face off against a Lions defense that has surrendered an NFL-high 299.3 passing yards per game through three contests. Young will profile as a strong fantasy option this week, even while the status of one of his top pass-catching weapons in wideout Jalen Coker (quadriceps) remains somewhat murky.

items.headline: Panthers' Bryce Young to Darren Waller has been money in red zone
items.summary: The veteran tight end's height, catch radius and history of red zone success make him a tough cover in big moments.

items.headline: Sources: Panthers RB Jonathon Brooks set for surgery, put on IR
items.summary: Panthers running back Jonathon Brooks is expected to undergo surgery to repair a core muscle injury and is set to miss at least six weeks, sources told NFL Network.

items.headline: The Panthers placed Brooks (core) on injured reserve Wednesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: As a result of the transaction, Brooks won't be eligible to play in any of the Panthers' next four games, but he's expected to miss additional time beyond that. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Wednesday that the running back will require surgery to repair a core muscle, which will keep him out for at least six weeks. With Brooks joining Trevor Etienne (ankle) on IR, AJ Dillon is left as the only reserve option on the 53-man roster behind lead back Chuba Hubbard. Carolina has Ahmani Marshall and Anthony Tyus on its practice squad, and the team will work out veteran Austin Ekeler on Wednesday and potentially sign him to bolster its running-back room, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston.

items.headline: Odunze secured three of six targets for 44 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.summary: Odunze was relegated to a complementary role in the 20-point victory, finishing fourth in receptions and third in both receiving yards and targets for the Bears on a night in which Case Keenum filled in for Caleb Williams (hamstring) under center. While Odunze entered the season as the presumptive No. 1 receiver, veteran offseason addition Kalif Raymond, who had familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's scheme from their mutual time with the Lions, has enjoyed an expanded role over the first three games while gathering in an impressive 19 of 21 targets. Conversely, Odunze is averaging a career-best 17.4 yards per reception but has a modest eight catches and no touchdowns through three games, numbers he'll look to boost during a Week 4 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Raymond caught six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown and recorded two punt returns for 15 yards in the Bears' 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday.
items.summary: Despite having three quarterbacks throwing him the ball in as many weeks, Raymond continues to be a top option for the Bears' receiving offense. The wide receiver was second in targets Monday night to only Luther Burden (11), who did not manage to exceed Raymond in yards. The returner's additional value on special teams just further adds to his offensive allure as the season continues.

items.headline: Higgins brought in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
items.summary: Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase turned in signature performances in the high-scoring loss, and the former finished as the runner-up in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day to his talented teammate. Higgins' first score of the season came on a difficult and contested 28-yard grab late in the first half, knotting the score at 17-17 going into halftime. Through three games, Higgins is on pace for a potential third career 1,000-yard season, as he's quickly amassed a 14-244-1 line on 23 targets.

items.headline: The Bengals signed Tinsley off the Texans' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: The Bengals needed to replenish their depth at wide receiver due to the injury absences of Andrei Iosivas (thumb, IR) and rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young (knee), the latter of whom has already been ruled out for Week 4 against the Jaguars. Tinsley appeared in 17 regular-season games for the Bengals in 2025, finishing with an 8-117-2 receiving line on 24 targets, though he joined the Texans' practice squad Sept. 1 after failing to make Cincinnati's 53-man roster at the end of training camp. Now that he's back with the Bengals, Tinsley will contribute both on special teams and in a rotational role on offense.

items.headline: Bengals cut WR Ke'Shawn Williams after costly muffed punt
items.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals cut WR Ke'Shawn Williams after he muffed a punt that eventually led to the Pittsburgh Steelers' 30-27 win. On Tuesday, Cincinnati signed WR Mitch Tinsley.

items.headline: The Bengals placed Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Iosivas is having surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, necessitating his move to injured reserve. As such, he will not be allowed to play for at least the next four games, so the earliest Iosivas can return is Week 8 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 1. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins will continue to serve as the Bengals' top pass catchers, but in Iosivas' absence, there are more offensive snaps available for rookie fourth-rounder Colbie Young, Dohnte Meyers and Ke'Shawn Williams.

items.headline: Sources: Bengals' Andrei Iosivas expected to miss 4-6 weeks
items.summary: Bengals wide receiver Andrei Iosivas is expected to miss four to six weeks because of a thumb injury, sources told ESPN.

items.headline: Boston caught two of four targets for 41 yards during the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion.
items.summary: The rookie second-rounder was held without a catch until the fourth quarter, when he caught 28- and 13-yard passes from Deshaun Watson before the duo connected on a two-point conversion late in the fourth quarter to extend the Browns' lead to three points. Boston was unable to record a touchdown catch for a third-straight game, though he still finished Sunday's contest as the Browns' second-leading receiver behind tight end Harold Fannin (51). Boston, Fannin and rookie first-rounder KC Concepcion will continue to serve as Watson's top targets in the passing game, with Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond working in rotation. Boston will take a 9-195-2 receiving line (on 15 targets) into Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers.

items.headline: Pickens caught seven of 11 targets for 82 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to Baltimore.
items.summary: The fifth-year wideout led the Cowboys in targets while setting new season highs in targets, catches and receiving yards, as he begins to shake off a slow start to the campaign. Pickens is still searching for his first TD of 2026, or even his first gain of 20-plus yards, but he'll look to continue building momentum in a Week 4 road trip to Houston.

items.headline: Cowboys' CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens playing with 'no egos'
items.summary: Lamb and Pickens believe their off-field connection is helping their on-field production.

items.headline: Mims (foot) is listed as inactive Sunday versus the Rams, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
items.summary: Despite being limited on all three of Denver's Week 3 practice reports, Mims will miss a second contest in a row due to a foot issue. His next chance to play is next Sunday at San Francisco. Kolbe Katsis likely will handle return duties in Mims' absence.

items.headline: Broncos rule out WR Marvin Mims Jr. (foot) for Sunday
items.summary: Denver Broncos wide receiver Marvin Mims Jr. will miss Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

items.headline: Waddle (leg) was on the field Wednesday for the start of the Broncos' practice session, Sam Jane of The Denver Post reports.
items.summary: Following Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams, Waddle was spotted wearing a walking boot on his right foot. His presence on the field begin Week 4 prep suggests he might have been wearing the boot as a precaution, but fantasy managers will nonetheless want to track Waddle's practice activity leading up to this weekend's game in San Francisco. Through his first three contests with the Broncos, Waddle has recorded 11 catches for 150 yards on 20 targets while carrying once for a 14-yard gain.

items.headline: Newcomers Jaylen Waddle, Jonah Coleman lead Broncos to win
items.summary: The Broncos mostly stood pat this offseason, keeping most of the 2025 roster together. But it was two newcomers on offense who helped them beat the Jaguars.

items.headline: LaPorta caught three of four targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
items.summary: The fourth-year tight end had his quietest game of the season, as five different Lions saw at least three targets from Jared Goff on the afternoon. LaPorta has been a complementary piece of an offense dominated by Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown in the early going, producing a 14-144-1 line on 19 targets through three contests. LaPorta will look to step up his numbers in Week 4 on the road against the Panthers.

items.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.

items.headline: St. Brown caught four of eight targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
items.summary: The star wideout tied Jahmyr Gibbs to lead the Lions in targets, but St. Brown did little with his volume aside from a four-yard TD strike from Jared Goff in the second quarter. It was still St. Brown's fifth score of the season in three games, to go along with 23 catches for 228 yards on 35 targets. He'll likely get plenty of looks from Goff again in Week 4 on the road against the Panthers.

items.headline: Williams caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets.
items.summary: The fifth-year wideout has watched Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown dominate the Lions' offense to begin the season, as that duo has combined for 11 total touchdowns -- including four in Sunday's win -- while Williams is still looking to make his first trip to the end zone in 2026. Williams will take a 10-137-0 line on 17 targets into a Week 4 tilt on the road against the Panthers.

items.headline: Schultz caught all three of his targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: Schultz crashed back down to earth after recording 12 catches for 140 yards in the previous game. The Texans remained without top WR Nico Collins (hamstring), and only Xavier Hutchinson (51) had more receiving yards than Schultz as C.J. Stroud threw for just 167 yards in Sunday's loss. Schultz figures to remain among Stroud's top targets in Week 4 against the Cowboys, even if Collins comes back.

items.headline: Allen caught six of nine targets for 63 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Allen was able to take advantage of the absence of Alec Pierce (heel) in Week 3, matching his season-high six receptions while notching his first touchdown of the year in the second quarter on a six-yard pass from Daniel Jones. With Pierce set to miss extended time, Allen will have a chance to carve out a significant role for himself as a reliable option for Indianapolis.

items.headline: Sources: Colts' Keenan Allen faces minimum 3-game suspension
items.summary: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen, who was formally charged last week with two misdemeanor offenses stemming from his drunken driving arrest in downtown Indianapolis last month, is facing a minimum three-game suspension, sources told ESPN.

items.headline: Josh Downs weighs in on risks of playing in NFL
items.summary: Josh Downs weighs in on risks of playing in NFL

items.headline: Downs caught five of 11 targets for 77 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win over Houston.
items.summary: Downs garnered the most targets on the team, narrowly edging out tight end Tyler Warren (10), while his 77 receiving yards led the way for Indianapolis. With Alec Pierce (heel) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Downs appears to have taken command as the team's No. 1 option at wide receiver. Over three games to open the regular season, the wideout has reeled in 14 of 24 targets for 186 yards, and he'll look to secure his first touchdown of the season in Week 4 against the Commanders.

items.headline: Slayton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans.
items.summary: Slayton signed with the Colts on Monday, two weeks after being released by the Giants. The move was to bolster Indianapolis' depth at wide receiver due to the absence of Alec Pierce (heel, IR). However, Slayton is not quite ready to make his Colts' debut, and his next opportunity to do so is Week 4 against the Commanders on Sunday, Oct. 4. The Colts will roll with six active wide receivers Sunday in Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

items.headline: Sources: Alec Pierce out weeks; Darius Slayton to join Colts
items.summary: Colts WR Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks because of a heel injury but will attempt to avoid surgery in the hopes of returning midseason.

items.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
items.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.

items.headline: Taylor rushed 23 times for 68 yards while catching two of three targets for four yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Taylor racked up 25 touches as the Colts notched their first win of the season, but he failed to find much running room against Houston's stout front. He finished with a season-low 72 scrimmage yards and failed to score after opening the season with a pair of two-touchdown performances. The workhorse running back is averaging 25 touches per game heading into the Colts' Week 4 trip to London to take on the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and Taylor's poised for another busy outing in the overseas clash between 1-2 teams.

items.headline: Warren caught nine of 10 targets for 55 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Texans.
items.summary: Warren failed to score a touchdown for the first time this season but set a new career high in catches while seeing plenty of involvement as a pass catcher in the absence of wide receiver Alec Pierce (heel), who was placed on IR after exiting early in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City. The second-year tight end is poised to maintain a prominent role when the Colts travel to London to face the Commanders in Week 4.

items.headline: Bhayshul Tuten continues to showcase his fantasy potential
items.summary: Bhayshul Tuten continues to showcase his fantasy potential

items.headline: Tuten rushed 15 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars' 35-6 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.summary: Serving as the clear lead back once again, Tuten proved himself worthy of the role with a crisp performance that saw him consistently generate useful gains versus a talented Patriots front seven. He capped off his fantasy-friendly effort with his second rushing touchdown of the campaign, a one-yard run with just over eight minutes remaining to close out the scoring on the afternoon. Tuten is averaging an impressive 4.7 yards per carry and a solid 16.0 touches through three games, rendering him an appealing option in all formats heading into a Week 4 road showdown against the Bengals next Sunday.

items.headline: Johnson carried the ball six times for 17 yards and returned one kickoff for 31 yards in Kansas City's 24-10 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: Johnson played 13 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The rookie fifth-rounder continues to give Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker an occasional breather, but Johnson's role on offense doesn't figure to expand beyond that without an injury to the former Seahawk.

items.headline: Chiefs' rookies eager for more success after opener
items.summary: Mansoor Delane, R Mason Thomas, Emmett Johnson, Peter Woods and Kahlil Benson must do it again vs. Indy.

items.headline: Rice caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
items.summary: Rice was the only Kansas City pass catcher with more than three targets, and he paced the team in receiving yards as well, but Patrick Mahomes' two touchdown passes went to Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce. Rice's target total has climbed from two in Week 1 to six in Week 2 and now nine in Week 3, so his usage has been trending in the right direction ahead of a Week 4 road game against the Raiders. He averaged 9.8 targets per game in eight appearances last season.

items.headline: Cousins completed 22 of 33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 35-27 win over the Saints. He added three rushing yards on three carries.
items.summary: The veteran QB got his first chance to work with Brock Bowers, but it was Michael Mayer and Cody White who were on the other end of Cousins' first two TDs of the afternoon before he connected with his superstar tight end for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter that provided the game-winning points. Cousins has led the Raiders to a stunning 3-0 record to begin the season, completing 67.4 percent (62-for-92) of his passes for 661 yards with a 9:3 TD:INT, and 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza could be waiting a while before he gets a chance to make his first NFL start. Cousins will face a much tougher test in Week 4 at home against Kansas City.

items.headline: Kirk Cousins' 'phenomenal' play has new-look Raiders at 2-0
items.summary: Kirk Cousins has done more than just help the Raiders transition through a rebuilding process after two games, leading Las Vegas to its first 2-0 record since 2021.

items.headline: Why Omarion Hampton was so disappointing in fantasy in Week 3
items.summary: Why Omarion Hampton was so disappointing in fantasy in Week 3

items.headline: Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: The Chargers' No. 1 back got seven more carries than change-of-pace option Keaton Mitchell, but he was able to outpace the latter by only four yards. It was a disappointing downturn for Hampton, who'd broken out with 94 rushing yards and a touchdown while adding a 2-21-0 receiving line against the Raiders in Week 2. The Chargers are now alarmingly 0-3 heading into a daunting Week 4 road matchup against the Seahawks, but Hampton figures to remain in a clear-cut lead role for that contest.

items.headline: Adams caught seven of 13 targets for 137 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: Adams continued to thrive as Matthew Stafford's top target in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip). During Nacua's two-game absence, Adams has compiled 15 catches for a whopping 332 yards and two touchdowns. Adams led the NFL with 14 touchdown receptions during the 2025 regular season and is showing no signs of slowing down at age 33 early in the 2026 campaign. He is poised to maintain a prominent role in Week 4 against the Eagles, though the Rams are optimistic that Nacua could be cleared to return by then.

items.headline: Don't be surprised if ... Kelce, Adams keep turning back the clock, Herbert rebounds
items.summary: Eric Karabell provides a list of what to watch for in fantasy football, so don't be surprised if any of these come true.

items.headline: Corum rushed six times for 15 yards and caught two of four targets for no gain during Sunday night's 30-26 loss to Denver.
items.summary: Corum saw nine less carries than backfield mate Kyren Williams in Week 3, the widest discrepancy between the two in a contest so far this season. Corum did get his highest amount of targets in a contest since he logged four targets against the Colts in Week 4 of the 2025 campaign, though he didn't really do much with his two catches Sunday. The running back has now rushed 28 times for 148 yards while catching three of five targets for 13 yards over three games to open the 2026 season.

items.headline: The Rams are better when both RBs get the ball
items.summary: Through two weeks, Williams and Corum have nearly split the carries exactly.

items.headline: Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards while catching six of seven targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-26 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: Williams was far more effective than Blake Corum, who turned six carries and four targets into just 15 scrimmage yards. Williams' season-opening touchdown streak came to a halt at two games, but he has been one of the league's top all-around performers at running back in the early going, averaging 5.6 yards per carry while catching 11 of 12 targets and scoring a touchdown apiece as a rusher and a receiver. The Rams are off to a 1-2 start heading into a Week 4 trip to Philadelphia, so expect Los Angeles to continue leaning heavily on its top backfield option in an effort to avoid losing more ground in the NFC standings.

items.headline: Henderson rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in his only target for six yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.summary: Playing in his second game of the season, Henderson led the Patriots in carries and rushing yards, yet each of those figures were only one more than those generated by backfield mate Rhamondre Stevenson. Henderson had a much more efficient showing in his Week 2 season debut with a 16-carry, 76-yard, one-touchdown showing against the Steelers, but game script had a significant impact on the volume for both of the Patriots' backs Sunday. Henderson will look to get back on track in a key Week 4 road divisional matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

items.headline: Patriots' TreVeyon Henderson says he's 'ready to go' for Week 2
items.summary: Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson said Thursday he's "ready to go" for Sunday's game against the Steelers after missing New England's opener with an ankle injury.

items.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. to sit with hamstring injury
items.summary: Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. will miss time with a hamstring injury suffered in Sunday's loss to the Raiders. New Orleans coach Kellen Moore did not specify how long Etienne will be out.

items.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne will have some "time lost" due to the hamstring injury he sustained in Sunday's 35-27 loss to the Raiders, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: Moore noted that a specific timeline for Etienne's return hasn't been established, making it uncertain whether or not the running back will be able to avoid a stint on injured reserve. At the very least, Etienne will be sidelined for the Saints' Week 4 game against the Falcons next Monday, which likely paves the way for Alvin Kamara to take on an expanded profile in the backfield after working in a complementary role the previous two weeks. Reserve backs Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson also should be in store for more opportunities for however long Etienne is out.

items.headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 39 yards Sunday in a loss to Las Vegas.
items.summary: Tyler Shough had another big day at quarterback for the Saints, with 160 of his 255 passing yards going to the combination of No. 1 wideout Chris Olave and top tight end Juwan Johnson. Vele finished third behind that duo in both targets (six) and receiving yards (39). The third-year wideout has been locked into a key role in the Saints' passing game, and through three contests he's registered 15 catches on 22 targets for 172 yards and one touchdown.

items.headline: Giants release fan favorite Odell Beckham Jr.
items.summary: The Giants released veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday.

items.headline: The Giants released Beckham on Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Beckham's second stint in New York will end with a whimper, as he failed to haul in his lone target while playing just 20 total snaps over the Giants' first three games of the season. Since the 33-year-old wasn't able to earn consistent snaps in the receiver rotation and didn't contribute on special teams, the Giants deemed him an expandable piece. Beckham will look to find work elsewhere, but he could struggle to land with a team willing to give him meaningful playing time.

items.headline: Skattebo carried the ball 20 times for 60 yards and caught three of four targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans.
items.summary: With Jameis Winston under center instead of Jaxson Dart (knee), the Giants leaned a little more heavily on their backfield and Skattebo saw a season high in touches while hitting for 100-plus scrimmage yards for the first time in 2026. The second-year back's longest play came on a 30-yard toss in the first quarter, as he made himself available downfield to bail out a scrambling Winston. Through three games, Skattebo is showing no ill effects from the ankle injury that ended his rookie campaign early, and he's collected 177 rushing yards and a TD on 50 carries while adding a 7-59-0 line on eight targets. He figures to see a big workload again in Week 4 at home against the Cardinals.

items.headline: Cam Skattebo reclaims role as Giants' feature back
items.summary: Just like that, it's business as usual for the bruising running back as he dominated the field in Week 1 against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Allen and Isaiah Davis will man the Jets backfield for as long as Breece Hall (thigh) is potentially sidelined, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Hall exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss at Detroit due to a thigh injury, and afterward he relayed that he "felt something" while running, per Brian Costello of the New York Post. Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter of ESPN then reported Monday that Hall is considered week-to-week. While Hall hasn't outright been ruled out for Week 4 or beyond, Allen currently ranks second on the team in carries with 19, which have gone for 61 yards, while Davis hasn't logged an offensive snap through three contests to begin the season. As a result, Allen is the better bet to take advantage of an absent Hall, if that comes to pass.

items.headline: Jets sign ex-Titans QB Will Levis, release Bailey Zappe
items.summary: The Jets have signed former Titans starting QB Will Levis to their practice squad and have released Bailey Zappe.

items.headline: Levis agreed Tuesday to sign with the Jets' practice squad, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
items.summary: The Jets will cut Bailey Zappe from their practice squad and have Levis replace him in their quarterback room. A 2023 second-round pick, the 27-year-old Levis was waived by the Titans at the end of the preseason after he completed 61.0 percent of his passes for 7.0 yards per attempt and a 21:16 TD:INT, to go with 240 rushing yards and a TD on 70 carries, across 21 starts over his first three seasons in the NFL.

items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Mitchell (finger) won't practice Wednesday and is considered week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Mitchell sat out the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3 due to the finger injury, and his absence to begin Week 4 prep in addition to Glenn classifying him as week-to-week rather than day-to-day suggests that the receiver is trending toward another absence this Sunday versus the Bears. If Mitchell ends up sitting out a second straight game, Isaiah Williams would be in store for another elevated snap count as the Jets' No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson.

items.headline: Jets without WR Adonai Mitchell (finger) vs. Lions
items.summary: Jets wide receiver Adonai Mitchell is inactive Sunday because of a finger injury.

items.headline: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: In his first action of the season, Shepard played 30 of 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Lions, turning his only target into a three-yard reception. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) battling an injury, Shepard could again be elevated ahead of next Sunday's game against the Bears. He has no fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Jets elevate Sterling Shepard with Adonai Mitchell in question
items.summary: The Jets promoted veteran Sterling Shepard from the practice squad, as starting WR Adonai Mitchell is questionable with a finger injury, and three other Jets receivers are on injured reserve.

items.headline: Week 3 winners and losers: Gibbs and JSN stay hot; St. Brown and Taylor go quiet
items.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs and Jaxon Smith-Njigba came up big in Week 3, while Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jonathan Taylor had very quiet days.

items.headline: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
items.summary: The veteran QB was almost flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

items.headline: Taylor (thumb) will not practice Wednesday and remains week-to-week, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Taylor appears set to miss a second straight game Sunday against the Bears. With Taylor out last Sunday against the Lions, first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq played a season-high 57.6 percent of the Jets' offensive snaps and posted a 7-105-1 receiving line on eight targets. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) also week-to-week for Gang Green, Sadiq has a path to once again play a prominent pass-catching role versus Chicago.

items.headline: Jets' No. 1 TE Mason Taylor (thumb) out vs. high-scoring Lions
items.summary: The Jets will be without No. 1 tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) and safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin) when they face the Detroit Lions on Sunday.

items.headline: Wilson caught 10 of 13 targets for 107 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-24 loss to Detroit.
items.summary: The star wideout -- who was evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return -- paced Jets pass catchers in all three receiving categories, and his 23-yard TD from Geno Smith in the fourth quarter tied the game at 24-24, only for the Lions to respond inside the final two minutes. It's Wilson's first 100-yard performance since Week 14 of the 2024 season, as injuries disrupted his 2025 campaign. Wilson also has found the end zone in back-to-back games, and he'll take a 21-243-2 line on 27 targets into a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

items.headline: Jets WR Garrett Wilson sheds slot, makes move back to outside
items.summary: Wilson hopes to avoid hits and be able to deliver more explosive plays on the perimeter.

items.headline: Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. put on IR with sprained ankle
items.summary: Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., one of the team's three first-round picks, has been placed on injured reserve with a sprained ankle.

items.headline: The Jets placed Cooper (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Cooper thus will miss at least the next four games after he suffered a sprained ankle in his pro debut this past Sunday in Tennessee. His next chance for game action will be a Week 6 road matchup with the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 18, and in the meantime, the Jets will operate with a receiving corps composed of Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith.

items.headline: Barkley rushed 15 times for 82 yards and secured one of two targets for minus-2 yards in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
items.summary: Barkley was a rare bright spot for an otherwise moribund Eagles offense, showing no ill effects from the stinger that cost him substantial time in a Week 2 win over the Titans. The star running back got his night started on the right foot with a 12-yard run on Philadelphia's opening possession and a nine-yarder on the second drive that was wiped out by a holding penalty. Barkley would go on to add another four rushes of seven or more yards, including a game-long 17-yard scamper. Barkley has yet to top 15 carries in any of the first three games of the season, but he's been highly efficient while averaging 5.1 yards per carry and posting four runs of 10-plus yards overall. Barkley and the Eagles have a tall order on their Week 4 ledger, however, as the Rams come to town Sunday.

items.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley to be 'fearless' vs. Bears despite stinger
items.summary: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley plans to play "fearless" Monday night against the Chicago Bears as he eyes a return from a stinger injury.

items.summary: Bears pick off Andy Dalton in the end zone

items.headline: Dalton is active as the Eagles' top backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
items.summary: After facing competition from Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton for the No. 2 job behind Jalen Hurts throughout training camp and the preseason, Dalton has emerged as the victor in the job battle. Dalton will suit up for the second week in a row, while McKee is inactive as the emergency No. 3 quarterback and Payton is also donning street clothes.

items.headline: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bears.
items.summary: Goedert was unable to practice all week due to an MCL sprain that he sustained during the Eagles' Week 2 win over the Titans. Zach Ertz was signed to the Eagles' practice squad Tuesday, and he figures to be elevated to the active roster for Monday's game and provide depth at tight end behind Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins. Goedert's next chance to play is Week 4 against the Rams on Sunday, Oct. 4, though he should be considered week-to-week.

items.headline: Eagles reuniting with Zach Ertz as Dallas Goedert has MCL sprain
items.summary: The Eagles are signing tight end Zach Ertz to their practice squad after the injury to starter Dallas Goedert and other injuries at the position.

items.headline: Wicks recorded two receptions for 32 yards on five targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Though he didn't find paydirt, Wicks played a critical role on the Eagles' lone scoring drive late in the second quarter, leading off the possession with a 13-yard catch and run. He was otherwise held in check while the game was still competitive, with his other reception coming in the fourth quarter when the Bears had built a 20-point lead. Through his first three games with Philadelphia, Wicks has produced a 9-179-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

items.headline: Freiermuth recorded two receptions for 30 yards on four targets and carried once for one yard in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
items.summary: Freiermuth took the field for 37 of the Steelers' 62 offensive snaps, with his 60 percent share placing him slightly behind fellow tight end Darnell Washington (47 snaps, 76 percent). The Steelers should continue to make ample use of two-tight-end sets to keep Freiermuth involved in their game plans, but since he doesn't project to see heavy target volume week to week, he'll remain a largely touchdown-dependent fantasy option.

items.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
items.summary: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."

items.headline: Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 10 yards in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
items.summary: After averaging just 5.2 yards per attempt while completing a sparse 59.5 percent of his passes over the first two games of the season, Rodgers begin clicking in Mike McCarthy's offense Sunday. The future Hall of Famer averaged 8.6 yards per attempt and had five completions of 22 yards or more while connecting with nine different pass catchers overall. Rodgers distributed the ball on his three touchdown passes as well, hitting Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and DK Metcalf from 38, 23 and six yards out, respectively. Rodgers' passing yardage total was a season high despite his completion total being his lowest through three games, and he'll look to carry the momentum into a Week 4 road matchup against an aggressive Browns defense on Thursday night.

items.headline: Jones did not attempt a pass and lost two yards on two end-of-game kneel-down plays during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Dolphins.
items.summary: The 49ers had no trouble building a comfortable lead throughout the contest, leading to Jones coming in to mop up over the final two series. The 28-year-old is coming off a sound 2025 campaign, throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions while completing a career-best 69.6 percent of his attempts. While Jones is considered one of the better backup quarterbacks in the NFL, his fantasy ceiling is virtually non-existent as long as Brock Purdy is healthy.

items.headline: Ranking all 32 backup NFL quarterbacks for the 2026 season
items.summary: We stacked the best No. 2 quarterbacks across the league, including Mac Jones and even a few backups who have already been forced to play in 2026.

items.headline: Inside George Kittle's 243-day recovery from torn Achilles
items.summary: Despite tearing his Achilles in the playoffs, Kittle appears to be back to his normal self. Here's how he won the recovery process.

items.headline: Kittle brought in six of seven targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Kittle led the 49ers in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon, marking what may have been his return to both full health and a full workload following last January's Achilles tear. The veteran tight end struck from 10 and 20 yards out for his pair of fourth-quarter scoring grabs, his first multi-TD tally since Week 11 of last season. Kittle now has hit or exceeded the 80-yard mark in consecutive games, and he should remain heavily involved in a Week 4 home matchup against a Broncos defense that tends to funnel passing toward the middle of the field due to its outstanding cornerback play.

items.headline: The 49ers placed Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Robinson was carted off the field due to a right ankle injury during San Francisco's Week 2 win against the Dolphins, after which coach Kyle Shanahan relayed that the wide receiver likely suffered a high-ankle sprain. On Monday, Shanahan said that Robinson was facing a recovery timeline of 3-to-6 weeks, so this move to injured reserve doesn't come as a surprise. Robinson will be first eligible to return to action Sunday, Oct. 25 in Atlanta, but with all of Christian Kirk (calf), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Ricky Pearsall (knee) and Robinson on IR, the 49ers will be going with Mike Evans (hip), Deebo Samuel, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge at wide receiver this Sunday against the Cardinals.

items.headline: 49ers lose another WR as Demarcus Robinson suffers ankle injury
items.summary: Demarcus Robinson's initial diagnosis was a high right ankle sprain, an injury that could cost him extended time.

items.headline: The 49ers placed Stribling (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Stribling suffered what appeared to be a serious non-contact injury during the 49ers' Week 1 win against the Rams in Melbourne, Australia, but afterward tests revealed that his left Achilles was intact, and eventually he was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle. After undergoing surgery, he's expected to miss roughly 10 weeks, meaning a move to IR was inevitable. At least during the initial weeks of Stribling's absence, Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins and KhaDarel Hodge will handle WR duties for San Francisco.

items.headline: 49ers' De'Zhaun Stribling has surgery, to miss about 10 weeks
items.summary: 49ers receiver De'Zhaun Stribling had surgery on his ankle and is expected to miss about 10 weeks, while tight end Jake Tonges has been ruled out for the season.

items.headline: Source: Niners signing veteran receiver Cooks to practice squad
items.summary: The Niners are signing free agent wideout Brandin Cooks to their practice squad, a source told ESPN on Tuesday.

items.headline: Cooks agreed Tuesday to sign with the 49ers' practice squad, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: San Francisco marks the eighth career stop for Cooks, who has racked up 9,811 receiving yards and 62 total touchdowns since entering the NFL as a first-round pick of the Saints in 2014. The 32-year-old will provide the 49ers with some much-needed depth after the WR depth chart was ravaged by injuries. Because he didn't participate in training camp with a team, Cooks could need time to regain conditioning and may not be ready to jump into action for a Week 3 game against the Cardinals. Expect him to be elevated from the practice squad or signed to the 49ers' 53-man roster once he's fully up to speed.

items.headline: Bucky Irving or Chase Brown in Week 4? Clay and Dopp debate the 2 RBs
items.summary: Bucky Irving or Chase Brown in Week 4? Clay and Dopp debate the 2 RBs

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said that Irving won't be included on the Buccaneers' Week 4 injury report, despite missing the final two possessions of Sunday's 23-16 loss to the Vikings, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Bowles didn't specify why Irving was off the field late in Sunday's contest, but any physical issue the running back might have been dealing with doesn't look like it will prevent him from playing Week 4. Despite logging a season-low 51 percent snap share, Irving still earned 17 touches (15 carries, two receptions) and accounted for 58 yards from scrimmage. He remains locked in as the clear No. 1 option out of the backfield over free-agent pickup Kenny Gainwell, who is averaging just 2.1 yards per carry and 3.7 yards per reception through three games.

items.headline: Spears (ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com reports.
items.summary: Coach Robert Saleh said there's no concern about Spears' availability for Sunday's game against Baltimore. Spears and Tony Pollard are dealing with ankle injuries and will be listed as DNP on Wednesday, but both are expected to be fine for Week 4. Spears rushed just three times for five yards last Sunday against the Giants and wasn't targeted in the passing game. Pollard handled 21 total opportunities, making Spears nothing more than a bench stash in fantasy.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups for Week 3: Stroud, Wicks, Spears among top options
items.summary: If injuries or tough matchups have you seeking help, Matt Bowen provides options at each key position.

items.headline: Ekeler signed a one-year contract with the Commanders on Tuesday, Zach Selby of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Ekeler will make his return to Washington for a third season, after his 2025 campaign came to an end after just two games due to a torn Achilles tendon. The 31-year-old received full medical clearance in the spring but remained unsigned through the first three weeks of the season before getting added to a Washington running-back room that includes Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White and rookie Kaytron Allen. With White having established himself as the Commanders' top pass-catching/change-of-pace option out of the backfield, Ekeler may struggle to carve out a consistent role on offense.

items.headline: Commanders set to re-add Austin Ekeler to RB room, sources say
items.summary: The Commanders are expected to sign free agent running back Austin Ekeler to their 53-man roster, pending a physical, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

items.headline: Marcus Mariota, in for hurt Jayden Daniels, leads Commanders
items.summary: Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota, subbing for the injured Jayden Daniels, reminded the NFL that the organization has another former Heisman Trophy winner -- and former No. 2 pick -- who can still play.

items.headline: Mariota completed 19 of 31 passes for 183 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seahawks. He added 11 rushing yards on five carries.
items.summary: The veteran quarterback got his first start in place of Jayden Daniels (elbow) and while Mariota didn't produce a lot of yardage against one of the top defenses in the league, he came up big when it counted, Mariota found Rachaad White for a six-yard score and Treylon Burks for an 11-yard TD in the first quarter before connecting with Terry McLaurin for a 30-yard touchdown in the third. Daniels could be back as soon as Week 5, but Mariota will get at least one more start, at home in Week 4 against the Colts.

items.headline: Who will find the end zone? Top predicted TD scorers for Week 4
items.summary: Mike Clay reveals his top predicted Week 4 TD scorers, including Derrick Henry, Kenneth Walker III and more.

items.headline: Ravens' Henry: 'Always love' for Titans, but not much this Sunday
items.summary: Ravens RB Derrick Henry faces his former team, the Titans, on Sunday for the first time since leaving Tennessee after the 2023 season. He said it's "always love" for the Titans, just not much when they play on Sunday.

items.headline: Allgeier rushed twice for minus-1 yard and caught all four of his targets for 10 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love worked as the clear lead back for the first time in his nascent career Sunday, relegating Allgeier to a minor role. Allgeier was thus limited to screen passes and checkdowns, catching everything thrown his way for minimal gains. It remains to be seen if Sunday's notable shift in workload will have carryover into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants on Sunday.

items.headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the 49ers on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: Beck will once again be the Cardinals' emergency QB3, meaning he won't be allowed to play Sunday unless both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Bourne hauled in two passes on three targets for 22 yards during the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Bourne's first target of the game came early in the first quarter, but he wasn't looked at by Jacoby Brissett again until late in the fourth, when the duo connected on passes of 14 and eight yards on back-to-back plays to set up a one-yard touchdown run by the QB. Bourne played 48 of 87 offensive snaps (55.2 percent), which was third-most among Cardinals wide receivers behind Michael Wilson (81) and Marvin Harrison (67). Bourne is up to a 12-108-0 receiving line on 14 targets through three regular-season games, ahead of Harrison in target volume but well behind Wilson and Trey McBride. Up next is a Week 4 road tilt against the Giants this Sunday.

items.headline: Brissett completed 38 of 52 passes for 280 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed four times for four yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Brissett put together one of his signature stat lines, parlaying massive passing volume into a solid yardage figure while remaining free of turnovers. The veteran signal-caller's pass-distribution profile also was on brand, as a whopping 28 of his pass attempts went in the direction of Michael Wilson (17 targets) and Trey McBride (11 targets). Brissett hit Wilson (five yards) and Jeremiyah Love (one yard) for his pair of touchdown passes, marking his first multi-TD tally of the season. Brissett is averaging a typically conservative 5.6 yards per attempt over his first three games, but he's thrown for over 275 yards twice to date heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

items.headline: McBride brought in nine of 11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: The talented tight end filled his usual workhorse role, finishing second in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Cardinals behind Michael Wilson. The chemistry between McBride and Jacoby Brissett is extremely well-established after nearly a season working together, and the former already has a 26-211-2 line on 34 targets through only three games, recording at least eight receptions and logging no fewer than 10 targets in each contest. McBride will continue to offer perhaps the best floor of any player at his position in a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

items.headline: Virgil (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: The rookie fifth-rounder has been a healthy scratch for each of the Cardinals' first two games of the regular season, and the next chance for him to make his NFL debut is Week 3 against the 49ers on Sept. 27. The Cardinals will go with six active wide receivers Sunday, with the position group led by Michael Wilson, Marvin Harrison and Kendrick Bourne.

items.headline: Wilson secured 11 of 17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Wilson's afternoon was reminiscent of several of those in his 2025 campaign, as the veteran receiver garnered a bulk of Jacoby Brissett's attention in his short- and mid-range role while leading the team in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Marvin Harrison was a bit more involved Sunday with three catches for 40 yards on five targets, but it appears clear Wilson and Trey McBride have far and away the most chemistry with Brissett. Wilson will take an 18-163-1 line on 31 targets into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

items.headline: Branch caught one pass on two targets for seven yards while logging an 18-yard punt return and a 22-yard kickoff return during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: The rookie third-rounder has contributed on both special teams as a returner and on offense as a rotational pass catcher. He's up to three catches (on four targets) for 21 yards and 110 return yards through three regular-season games. His involvement on offense hasn't been as high as other rookie wide receivers, but the Falcons appear committed to using Branch in multiple ways to utilize his speed and explosiveness.

items.headline: Dotson caught one pass on three targets for 11 yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: Dotson's three targets from Michael Penix were actually second-most on the Falcons behind Drake London (10), with Dotson finishing tied for the third-most receiving yards on the team. He's played over 60 percent of offensive snaps in each of the first three games of the regular season but has a 4-41-0 receiving line (on 11 targets) to show for it. That said, Dotson's scoring floor could steadily increase as the season progresses and Penix gets more reps under his belt. The Falcons will stay on the road for a Week 4 NFC South tilt against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

items.headline: Hooper caught both of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown during Atlanta's 35-14 win over Green Bay on Thursday.
items.summary: Hooper was on the field for 16 of the Falcons' 71 offensive snaps, which was behind fellow tight ends Charlie Woerner (43), Kyle Pitts (42) and Nick Muse (17). However, unlike those three tight ends, Hooper contributed to the scoreboard by hauling in a five-yard touchdown pass from Michael Penix with just over a minute left to play in the second quarter. Hooper has a 4-31-1 receiving line (on six targets) through the first three games of the regular season.

items.headline: Muse (shoulder) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: Muse popped up on Monday's estimated practice report due to a shoulder injury, but he was cleared to participate fully in Tuesday's practice and is on track to play against the Packers on Thursday. The fifth-year tight end has contributed on both offense as a blocker and on special teams, though he's yet to record a target through two regular-season games.

items.headline: Robinson rushed 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 54 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: Robinson's backfield mate Bijan Robinson and No. 1 receiver Drake London stole the show Thursday while accruing 194 yards apiece, but Brian had his own moment in the spotlight when he capped off a 10-play, 92-yard drive in the third quarter with a seven-yard touchdown run. Brian Robinson now has back-to-back games with double-digit carries and has at least 50 rushing yards in each, keeping him somewhat relevant in very deep formats heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

items.headline: Strand (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Packers.
items.summary: Strand saw some action in relief of Cooper Rush in the 34-3 loss to Carolina in Week 2. However, he didn't play well, throwing for 59 yards and one interception off 8-for-15 passing, adding two carries for 16 yards. With Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) back in the mix, and Rush serving as the emergency signal-caller, Strand's services won't be needed in Week 3.

items.headline: Zaccheaus brought in both of his targets for nine yards and returned one punt for four yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
items.summary: Both of Zaccheaus' catches occurred in the second quarter on the same drive, which ended with a 44-yard field goal by Nick Folk. Zaccheaus is up to four catches (on six targets) for 17 yards through three regular-season games while operating as a depth option in the passing game, though Thursday's win may have been the start for a more explosive offense for the Falcons with Michael Penix under center, rather than Tua Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (coach's decision) or Jack Strand (coach's decision). The Falcons will travel to New Orleans to face the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

items.headline: The Falcons signed Herbert to the practice squad Wednesday, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: Herbert entered the league in 2021 and has suited up for the Bears, Bengals and Jets. In 63 regular-season games, the 28-year-old amassed 1,957 yards and nine touchdowns off 416 carries, adding 54 catches for 316 yards and two touchdowns. While the Falcons have Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson in the backfield, Herbert could be elevated if one of those players gets hurt down the line.

items.headline: Andrews caught three of five targets for 24 yards during Sunday's 34-31 win over the Cowboys.
items.summary: Andrews was limited by a hand injury that he suffered in the second quarter, and he was on the field for only 33 of the team's 64 offensive snaps. The tight end has recorded at least three catches in each of the team's first three games, reeling in 13 of 18 targets for 122 yards so far this season. Andrews has yet to reach the end zone this year, and his next chance will come against the Titans in Week 4.

items.headline: Fagnano (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Dallas but will be available as the team's emergency quarterback if needed.
items.summary: Fagnano was also the Ravens' emergency signal-caller for the first two games of the 2026 campaign. That trend will likely continue as long as Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are available.

items.headline: Hill rushed twice for six yards and caught two targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 24-17 loss to the Saints.
